claim: Task Abstention (May 2026) provides a distribution-free, calibrated whole-task abstention rule for code generation using multiple hypothesis testing over execution-outcome consistency across sampled completions, without requiring oracle test cases.
stance_target: novelty of any distribution-free/conformal abstention or risk-control mechanism for code generation at the PROBLEM level
scope_conditions: whole code-generation task granularity, open-source code LLMs, May 2026
quoted_support: We prove that our approach provides a rigorous, distribution-free theoretical guarantee on its abstention decisions.

claim: Task Abstention treats an entire code-generation task as a single pass/fail hypothesis and does not decompose risk across sub-requirements or individual unit tests within one task.
stance_target: per-requirement conformal risk control for code remaining open despite Task Abstention
quoted_support: determining whether a given LLM should abstain from performing a specific code generation task to avoid likely hallucination
